Computer Graphics Tools

Computer Graphics
❖   Various ways to define Computer Graphics (CG)
▪ It is broadly referring to the field of study that deals with the display 
mechanism of a computer.
▪ Display mechanism may be hardware related (CRT/LED/Plasma Monitor) 
and/or software (CAD-computer-aided-design, TDI-Thompson Digital Image 
software, etc.) related .
▪ Computer graphics is the branch of computer science that deals with 
generating images with the aid of computers (Wikipedia).
▪ Computer graphics is an art of drawing pictures, lines, charts, etc. using 
computers with the help of programming.
▪ The technology dealing with the generation of pictures, designs, etc. on a 
computer.
▪ An example of computer graphics is the design of pictures and scenes on a 
computer game.

Now-a-days Computer Graphics is used in many 
of our day-to-day applications 
▪ Engineering : virtual reality, design of buildings, automobiles, 
aircraft, and so on
▪ Industries
▪ Entertainment 
▪ Art
▪ Education
▪Advertisement, and many more…..

Applications of CG-Presentation Graphics
❖ Computer Graphics are used to plot bar charts, line graphs, pie charts and 
other displays showing relationships between multiple parameters. 
❖ These graphs (visual representations) give better understating of 
data/observations. 
❖ Used to summarize: Financial Reports, Statistical Reports, Mathematical 
Reports, Scientific Reports, Economic Data for research reports, Managerial 
Reports, and so on.

❖ AutoCAD is a commercial computer-aided design and drafting software 
application developed and marketed by Autodesk.

designers, and many others.
❖ Corel DRAW : It is a vector graphics editor developed and marketed by Corel

graphics-related programs. 
Applications of CG-Educational Software

❖  Graphical Kernel System (GKS) : It was the first ISO standard for low-level 
computer graphics, introduced in 1977.
❖ GKS provides a set of drawing features for two-dimensional vector graphics 
suitable for charting and similar duties 
❖PHIGS (Programmer's Hierarchical Interactive Graphics Standard) is an 
application programming interface (API) standard for rendering 3D computer 
graphics. 
❖ It is mainly the extended 3D-version of Graphical Kernel System (GKS) 
system. 
❖ Computer Graphics Metafile (CGM): It is a free and open international 
standard file format for 2D vector graphics, raster graphics, and text.
Applications of CG-Educational Software

❖ Computer-generated imagery (CGI) is the application of computer graphics 
to create or contribute to images in art, printed media, video games, films, 
television programs, shorts, commercials, videos, and simulators. 
❖It can also be used for 3-D computer graphics for creating characters, scenes 
and special effects in films and television, which is described as 'CGI 
animation'.

❖Rendering or image synthesis is the process of generating a photorealistic or non-
photorealistic image from a 2D or 3D model by means of a computer.
❖ Non-photorealistic rendering – rendering of scenes in an artistic style, intended to 
look like a painting or drawing

▪1) Shading – how the color and brightness of a surface varies with lighting
▪2) Texture-mapping – a method of applying detail to surfaces
▪3) Shadows – the effect of obstructing light

Output of a Computer Graphics System
❖ Synthesize image on a computer screen. 
▪ An image consists of different types of primitive objects (lines, circles, 
rectangles, and so on). 
▪ Objects are filled (presented) with different colors / styles / textures, and 
so on. This process is called rendering.
▪ The images can be manipulated with the help of input devices such 
mouse, keyboard, joystick, etc.

Computer Graphics vs. AI Generated Images
Computer Graphics
❖ Computer Graphics focuses on constructing 
scenes using mathematical models, geometry, 
rendering, and physical principles.
❖It is based on geometric modelling, physics, 
lighting, and rendering equations.
AI Generated Image
❖Creation of images using machine 
learning/Deep learning models trained on 
large image datasets.
❖Based on learned statistical patterns from 
millions of training images.
